fields.text: For Spaceghost (Josh may relay): confirm or change the next bucket (portable host contract, authenticated grant issuance, physical GPU validation on the RTX 4090 here), the Genode monitor layout, the Unikraft ingress transport, the Windows machine, and Drift's kernel timing.

Josh said go on the three-lane bucket, so item 1 is now a veto rather than a go: the plans for the portable host contract, authenticated grant issuance, and physical GPU validation are being written and the lanes start when they are reviewed. Items 2 to 5 still wait on you.

Correction: item 6 added, the buckets runtime (your 'datacentric Rust of sorts' idea). My earlier repository note had misread q6 as a question about which changes come next; that was wrong and is fixed in docs/superpowers/records/spaceghost-questions.md.
Item 7 added: two authority rulings the lane plans made (single-use approvals; delegation never changes the effective subject). The three lanes are running on them; veto if wrong.

All three lanes of the bucket have landed on master (grant issuance 1014, portable host contract section 1 to 1428 checks and 17 laws, physical GPU validation on the RTX 4090), so item 1 is moot. Items 2 to 7 still wait on you: the Genode monitor layout, the Unikraft ingress transport, the Windows machine, Drift timing, the buckets runtime questions, and the two authority rulings to veto. Nothing new is dispatched until you or Josh pick the next work.

Josh said go on a second bucket: add-linux-host section 1 (the first consumer of the host contract, on this host), add-policy-aware-audit, and add-executor-rendezvous (Bend only). Plans are being written. Items 2 to 7 still wait on you; the Windows and Drift hosts stay deferred until items 4 and 5 are answered.
Item 8 added: who approves audit event-read and export grants on a real host (the lane installs them from the monitor for now, recorded as a gap).
Item 9 added: rendezvous billing, quote as a ceiling (the plan's ruling) or exact.
Item 10 added: whether the new Linux broker should converge with the FUSE mounted-view canary later (section 1 keeps them separate).
